advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route bridge_sync's mutating pass through the same pause-check + pass-lock + heartbeat guard sequence used by main(), so it honors an active pause and cannot run concurrently with another pass.
evidence: _lib_ops.py:165-174 `orchestrator = _engine_module("rebar_reconciler.__main__")` then `result = orchestrator.run_pass_result(... target_mode=Mode.LIVE ... route=route)` — calls run_pass_result directly, not run_pass/main

__main__.py:629-707 main() performs `_pause_exit_code(...)`, `_post_pause_preflight`, `_resolve_held_lock`, `_acquire_or_adopt_pass_lock`, and starts the `_Heartbeat` — all only in the CLI orchestration path
reconcile.py:143-204 reconcile_once does fetch/diff/apply/persist and no lock or pause enforcement
ticket f789 AC: 'Each legacy library reconcile mode has the same semantic state and mutation outcome as its mapped new bridge operation' and prerequisite 1104 pause CAS
advisory.finding: bridge_sync() executes a mutating LIVE reconcile pass in-process via run_pass_result -> reconcile_once, bypassing the pass-lock acquisition, lock-steal resolution, heartbeat lease, and the pause (BRIDGE_PAUSED) check that main() applies for mutating passes. reconcile_once performs none of these itself, so bridge_sync can mutate Jira while a pause is active and without holding the reconciler lock — unlike the legacy reconcile('live') which runs through main() with the full guard sequence.
scenarios: Operator runs `rebar bridge pause`; an agent then calls rebar.bridge_sync() or the MCP bridge_sync tool and mutations are applied despite the active pause
Two concurrent bridge_sync callers (or one bridge_sync plus a running reconcile pass) proceed simultaneously because no pass lock is acquired

docs/mcp-reference.md claims bridge control/sync tools 'enforce Jira-sync authorization at call time' and release-notes.md claims the change retains read-only guarantees, but bridge_check_access does neither
blocking.finding: MCP tool `bridge_check_access` is registered as a read-only tool (annotation READ_ONLY_OPEN_WORLD) and placed before the `if not ctx.readonly()` guard, so it is exposed under REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 and never checks allow_jira_sync(); yet its implementation performs live Jira mutations (create issue, add label, write issue property, delete issue). A read-only / non-sync-authorized principal can therefore trigger remote Jira create/write/delete side effects.
scenarios: Operator runs the MCP server with REBAR_MCP_READONLY=1 expecting no mutations; an agent calls bridge_check_access and creates + deletes a Jira issue and writes labels/properties against the live Jira instance
Server without REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC=1 still permits live Jira writes via the access check
